newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end higher on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end higher on short-covering.

text.p: A late round of short-covering pushed most U.S. debt futures near the daily highs at the close, but contracts still remained within Friday's ranges, traders and analysts said.
December T-bonds rose to 108-28/32 late, near the day's high at 108-29/32, but below Friday's three-week high at 109-00.

Volume was lighter than normal in both bond and Eurodollar futures pits in what several traders described as "a typical session for Monday." But Friday's rally left traders and analysts bemused and sidelined on Monday.
"No one really knows what to do," one bond futures floor source said. "We had priced in a rate hike, but now we're pricing in the idea the Fed will do nothing."
While this week's schedule of economic data is light, traders and analysts said the market will be weighing every piece of data for signs of U.S. inflationary pressures.

August U.S. industrial production and capacity utilization reports will be released on Tuesday at 0915 EDT/1315 GMT. Production is seen rising 0.4 percent versus up 0.1 percent in July and utilization is seen at 83.3 versus 83.2.

"It is really close to an ideal, experimental situation for the opportunistic disinflation theory as anyone would have dreamed of," one analyst said, referring to a Fed study that was widely published in the summer and suggested greater leeway by the Fed when determining monetary policy.
On Friday afternoon, Federal Reserve governor Lawrence Lindsey said the Federal Reserve could not afford to wait until a pick-up in the inflation rate becomes evident before raising rates.
"Everything except prices appear to be on the move," the analyst said.
Traders and analysts said the decline in commodity prices, coupled with fairly good results of the Treasury department's three- and six-month bill auction led to late short-covering.

At the end of pit trade, December T-bonds were up 03/32 at 108-26/32, 10-year notes were up 01/32 at 107-02/32, March T-bills were unchanged at 94.59, December Eurodollars were up two basis points at 94.15, March Eurodollars were steady at 94.01, and munibonds were up 17/32 at 114-05/32.
